text:
WEEK 12 OF #SUNDAYSTOCKPICK

The First Humanoid Robot Stock Just Hit the Market. Revenue Is $1.8 Million. Orders Are $300 Million.

For eleven weeks, I have been building a portfolio around one idea. Own the companies that become essential when the world gets serious.

Week 10 was AST SpaceMobile, the connectivity layer that ties the world together. 
Week 11 was QuantumScape, the storage layer that makes the system work.

This week, I am going to the layer that replaces human labor entirely. The machine that picks up the box, moves the tote, and does the job that warehouses cannot fill.
And it just became the first pure-play humanoid robotics company to trade on a U.S. exchange.

Week 12: Agility Robotics (ticker: AGLT).
The stock closed its first day of trading at $11.51. 

By November 6, it had pulled back to roughly $9.90, giving the company a market capitalization near $482 million. The pre-money transaction valuation was $2.5 billion. The gap between the SPAC price and the aftermarket price tells you the market is still deciding what this company is worth.

That uncertainty is where the opportunity starts.

THE SETUP: WHY AGLT RIGHT NOW
Agility Robotics completed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on November 4, 2026, and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT on November 5. It is the first U.S.-listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments.

The deal brought in roughly $465 million in gross capital before expenses, a combination of $164 million from Churchill XI's trust account, a $201 million PIPE led by Foxconn, and $100 million in equity funding Agility had already received.

The company's strategic investors include Nvidia, Amazon, SoftBank, and Foxconn. That is not a list of tourists. Those are the companies that build the chips, run the warehouses, and fund the automation economy.

The bear case writes itself. Revenue in 2025 was $1.8 million. Net loss was $138.1 million. Operating cash consumption was $99.8 million. More than half of the 2025 revenue came from five robots purchased by one of its own investors. The company has warned that it expects additional losses and higher operating expenses for the foreseeable future.

The bull case is harder to dismiss. Agility has more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for its next-generation Digit 5 robot, subject to contractual milestones and final product specifications. Its robots have logged more than 65,000 hours of real-world operation. And it operates RoboFab, a 70,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Salem, Oregon, designed for annual production capacity of up to 10,000 robots.

That is not a slide deck. That is a factory, a field record, and an order book.

WHAT AGILITY ROBOTICS ACTUALLY DOES
Agility builds Digit, a two-legged humanoid robot with arms designed to pick up and move totes, containers, and other repetitive loads in warehouses and manufacturing facilities.

The Deployments
Digit is not a demo. It is working in customer facilities.

At GXO's Flowery Branch, Georgia, logistics site, Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes. GXO has expanded the agreement to two additional U.S. logistics facilities in Statesville, North Carolina, and Lebanon, Tennessee, expected to start in early 2027.

Digit is also deployed at Schaeffler, the German automotive and industrial supplier, and at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada. Agricultural equipment manufacturer AGCO has signed a commercial agreement for a Digit pilot at its Hesston, Kansas, facility, expected to begin in 2027.
Agility has deployed Digit at nine customer facilities in total, including sites operated by Amazon, Toyota, and GXO.

Digit 5
The next-generation robot, Digit 5, was unveiled in September 2026. It is designed to work alongside people without full safety cages, a change that matters enormously for warehouse operators who do not want to rebuild their floors.

Digit 5 stands 5 feet 11 inches tall and weighs 284 pounds. It can repeatedly lift up to 50 pounds, a 40% increase over the previous generation, and reach over seven feet high. It uses cycloidal actuator technology, interchangeable end effectors, and a triple-layer safety system that includes AI for spotting humans and triggering stops or evasive maneuvers.

The battery supports 90 minutes of operation and can recharge in nine minutes, enabling more than 20 hours of work in a 24-hour day.

Agility targets initial Digit 5 deliveries in the first half of 2027 and general availability by the end of 2027.

RoboFab
RoboFab is Agility's 70,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Salem, Oregon, designed for annual output of up to 10,000 robots. The company also has hardware and AI development operations in Fremont, California, and a planned 50,000-square-foot expansion in Pittsburgh.

That installed capacity is not current output. It is design capacity. But it tells you what Agility believes the demand curve looks like.

THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
Revenue Is Tiny, But the Order Book Is Not

2025 revenue was $1.8 million. Net loss was $138.1 million. Operating cash burn was $99.8 million. In the first half of 2026, revenue was $174,000 and losses reached $362 million, according to TechCrunch.

Those are the numbers the skeptics point to. They are real.

But the $300 million in committed multi-year Digit 5 orders is the number that changes the conversation. One customer has ordered 1,000 robots, with payments tied to use of the robots over three years and contingent on Agility meeting delivery deadlines and promised product features.

If Agility executes, that order book converts into revenue. If it does not, the milestones protect the customer.

The Capital Position
The $465 million gross capital gives Agility runway to build, deploy, and fulfill orders. The company has warned of continued losses, but the merger proceeds were explicitly raised to fund production and deployment expansion.

The Ownership Structure
Existing Agility shareholders rolled all their equity into the combined company. Their shares, along with those held by the Churchill sponsor, are subject to a 180-day lock-up after closing, with provisions for early release tied to stock-price performance.
That means the float is limited. The stock can move violently on relatively small volume. The first day of trading reflected that.

Analyst Coverage
There are no analyst price targets in the last three months. The banks have not published models yet. That is normal for a freshly de-SPACed company. It also means the stock is trading on narrative, not on consensus estimates. When coverage begins, the narrative will get a second look.

WHY THE STOCK IS VOLATILE (AND WHY THAT IS GOOD FOR YOU)
The first reason is the SPAC structure. Redemptions, lock-ups, and a limited float create price dislocations that have nothing to do with the business.

The second reason is the pre-revenue reality. Agility generated $1.8 million in revenue in 2025. The market has to believe the order book converts before it will pay a premium.

The third reason is the competition. Tesla is developing Optimus. Figure AI is privately valued at roughly $39 billion. Apptronik is privately valued at roughly $5.5 billion. Chinese manufacturers accounted for about 90% of humanoid robot shipments last year, according to Omdia. Unitree, a Chinese humanoid company, went public in Shanghai with a market value of about $40 billion.
The market is missing the distinction between a company that is early and a company that is failing.

Agility has a factory designed for 10,000 units. It has robots working in real facilities. It has $300 million in committed orders for the next-generation product. It has Nvidia, Amazon, Foxconn, and SoftBank on the cap table.
The stock is priced like a science project that ran out of cash. It is not that anymore.

THE RISKS (I AM NOT HERE TO SELL YOU A DREAM)
Execution risk is real. Digit 5 has not shipped commercially yet. The first deliveries are targeted for the first half of 2027. Any delay pushes revenue back.

Milestone risk is real. The $300 million in orders is subject to contractual milestones. If Agility misses a delivery deadline or a product specification, the customer can walk.
Cash burn risk is real. The company spent $99.8 million in 2025. It has $465 million in fresh capital. That is runway, but it is not infinite. If commercial revenue does not ramp before the capital runs low, dilution is the likely outcome.

Competition risk is real. Tesla, Figure, Apptronik, Unitree, and a dozen others are chasing the same market. Agility's edge is its deployment history and its U.S. manufacturing base. That edge has to hold.

ROI risk is real. GXO's CEO has said publicly that the company has not yet achieved ROI on humanoids and is a couple of years away. Agility claims a payback period of roughly 1.1 years on outright ownership, but that is Agility's math, not the customer's audited result.

Valuation risk is real. At $2.5 billion pre-money on $1.8 million of 2025 revenue, the valuation is a bet on the future, not a reflection of the present.
But here is my counter. RoboFab is built. Digit is working. The order book is $300 million. The capital is in the bank. And the first pure-play humanoid robotics listing in the U.S. gives public investors access to a category that was previously reserved for private markets.

HOW I AM PLAYING THIS
I am not a trader. I am an investor.

My plan for AGLT is straightforward.
Buy in the $8.50 to $10.50 range. Current levels are inside that band.

Hold for 36 to 48 months. This is not an 18-month trade. It is a bet on the 2027 commercial launch of Digit 5.

Target $18 to $22. That assumes the order book converts, RoboFab ramps, and the market begins to value Agility against the private humanoid valuations rather than the 2025 revenue line.

Add on dips toward $7.00 if the market gives them to me.
This is a smaller position than my defense picks and smaller than Oklo. The lock-up expiration, the cash burn, and the milestone risk mean the variance is enormous. Size it like a venture bet, not a core holding.

HOW THIS CONNECTS TO WEEKS 2 THROUGH 11

Look at the full board now.

Week 7 was Oklo, the power that runs the whole system. 
Week 8 was Joby, the transport that moves it all. 
Week 9 was IonQ, the compute layer that solves what classical machines cannot. 
Week 10 was AST SpaceMobile, the connectivity layer that ties the world together. 
Week 11 was QuantumScape, the storage layer that makes the system work.

Week 12 is Agility Robotics, the labor layer that does the work.

Oklo generates the power. QuantumScape stores it. AST moves the data. IonQ processes it. Agility moves the physical world.

Every warehouse needs hands. Every factory needs a shift that does not call in sick. Every logistics network needs a solution for the labor gap that is not a temporary fix.

Own the companies that cannot be replaced when the world gets serious.

BOTTOM LINE

Agility Robotics just became the first U.S.-listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments. The stock is trading near $10 after a volatile debut. The business reported $1.8 million in revenue in 2025 and a $138.1 million net loss. It also has more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5, more than 65,000 hours of real-world operation, a factory designed for 10,000 robots a year, and $465 million in fresh capital from a deal backed by Nvidia, Amazon, Foxconn, and SoftBank.

The market is pricing it like a pre-revenue SPAC that ran out of time. It is not that anymore. It is a company with a product, a factory, a field record, and an order book.

This is the kind of setup that separates good investors from great ones. Not because it is complicated. Because it is early, and most people are still looking at the revenue line instead of the robots moving totes in Georgia.

Next Sunday, Week 13 drops. Turn on notifications so you do not miss it.

If this post made you rethink what humanoid robotics means for the labor market, drop a like and repost it. It helps more than you know.

Follow @WallStreet2Web3  for more no BS stock analysis every Sunday.

Not financial advice. Do your own research. But also, $300 million in committed orders, 65,000 hours of operation, and a factory designed for 10,000 robots do not lie.

The House Voted 211-204 to Bury Hegseth's Impeachment

The House did not vote on whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth committed high crimes and misdemeanors, the Constitution's standard for removing a civil officer if two-thirds of the Senate later convicts. It voted to send the impeachment resolution to committee instead of judging the charges.

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican retiring in January after losing a primary President Trump backed, posted around 2:18 p.m. Mountain Time that the House was bringing up his eight articles and that a vote to derail them by referring them to committee was expected around 5:30 p.m. Eastern, 3:30 p.m. Mountain. The Clerk of the House logged roll call 317 at 6:02 p.m. Eastern, 4:02 p.m. Mountain.

A privileged impeachment resolution is a scheduling tool, not a legal finding. Because the Constitution gives the House the sole power to impeach, a member can force a floor vote within two legislative days. The House can then vote on the articles, table them and kill them immediately, or refer them to a committee. Referral does not declare the secretary innocent. It hands the papers to a chairman who can simply never schedule them.

Rep. Darrell Issa, a California Republican, moved to refer Massie's resolution, now numbered H. Res. 1655, to the House Judiciary Committee. The motion passed 211 to 204, with 18 not voting.
https://t.co/sQKCSgQtlj

A yea sent the case to committee. A nay would have left the House to deal with the articles on the floor. Republicans voted 210 to 1 to refer, with 7 not voting. Democrats voted 0 to 203 against referral, with 11 not voting. The one Independent on the roll, Rep. Kevin Kiley of California, voted yea. The only Republican nay was Massie. No Democrat voted to refer.

Rep. Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican and retired Air Force general, said he would not impeach because he wants to "win in Iran." Rep. Nancy Mace, a South Carolina Republican, said Hegseth "should not be the one scapegoated" for that war. Both voted yea, as did Idaho's Rep. Russ Fulcher and Rep. Mike Simpson.

In 2017 the House tabled privileged articles against President Trump from Rep. Al Green, a Texas Democrat, 364 to 58, with 4 present, on roll call 658. In 2019 it tabled Green's next attempt 332 to 95, with 1 present, on roll call 483.
https://t.co/mJFc3Vux4K
https://t.co/UyoI6sbgAV

Tabling is a clean kill. Referral is slower, and it is not always the end. On November 13, 2023, the House voted 209 to 201, roll call 645, to refer a privileged impeachment of Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas to committee. Eight Republicans joined every Democrat who voted that night. On February 13, 2024, the House impeached Mayorkas anyway, 214 to 213, and the Senate later dismissed the articles without a full trial.
https://t.co/7RYRQ0EMLw

Today's vote parks Massie's case for this Congress. CBS reported that Massie said Monday he would not bring another Hegseth resolution. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York Democrat who called himself a "hard yes" over the weekend, voted against referral. Democrats take both gavels on January 3, 2027, and can file new articles. Removal would still take about 67 Senate votes if all are present.
https://t.co/gdATaD0aM1

Hegseth this morning called the effort a "farce" and a "political spectacle." The eight articles cover unauthorized war in Iran and Yemen, the boat strikes, the raid that seized Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro, civilian harm, and alleged retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat.

A secretary should not be impeached merely because a war is unpopular, or merely because he carried out the President's orders. Whether those orders broke the War Powers Resolution is a separate question, and today's referral did not answer it.

I laid out all eight articles, the evidence and the administration's defense here:

November 10, 2017 — RJ Barrett committed to Duke 🔵😈

The 6’7” guard from Mississauga, Ontario, arrived in Durham as the No. 1 overall recruit in the 2018 class, according to 247Sports.

Barrett made an immediate impact during his freshman season, becoming one of the most dominant scorers in college basketball alongside teammate Zion Williamson.

He finished the season averaging 22.6 points per game, tying Williamson for the ACC scoring lead and making them the first freshman teammates in NCAA history to each average 20+ points in a season.

Barrett’s freshman season was filled with history:

860 points, setting the Duke and ACC freshman scoring records
Second-most points in a single season in Duke history, behind only JJ Redick’s 964
26 games with 20+ points, an ACC freshman record
38 consecutive games scoring in double figures, an ACC freshman record
402 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium, breaking JJ Redick’s single-season arena record
Started all 38 games and set the Duke freshman record for minutes played (1,341)

His season earned him some of the biggest honors in the country:

Consensus First Team All-American
USA Today National Player of the Year
Jerry West Award winner
First Team All-ACC
ACC All-Freshman Team
ACC All-Tournament Team
NCAA All-East Region Team

And the memorable performances just kept coming.

Barrett scored 33 points in his Duke debut against Kentucky in the Champions Classic, the most ever by a Duke freshman in a debut. He followed that up with another 33-point performance against North Carolina, setting the record for most points by a Duke freshman against the Tar Heels.

He also recorded the fourth triple-double in Duke history with 21 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists against NC State.

Barrett declared for the 2019 NBA Draft on April 10 and was selected No. 3 overall by the New York Knicks.

He joined Zion Williamson and Cam Reddish in the first round, marking just the second time in NBA Draft history that one college program had three players selected in the top 10.

One season. 860 points. A whole lot of records. RJ Barrett left his mark on Durham in a big way. 🔵😈

Secretary Hegseth Torches Baseless Impeachment Stunt: “This Is Not Patriotism; This Is Sabotage”

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

This morning, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth systematically dismantled the desperate, ego-driven impeachment hoax by a disgruntled and defeated Congressman. Secretary Hegseth made clear that every operation targeted in the eight articles was lawful, ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, properly notified to Congress, and carried out by warriors who delivered decisive results. He also made clear that this is not oversight; it is a political spectacle aimed at President Donald J. Trump and the men and women who defend our country.

• “What one disgruntled and defeated Congressman is attempting is not oversight and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment, timed for one man’s final days in Congress to try to do damage to this President, this country, and most irresponsibly, the Warriors who defend it. It’s a farce and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it.”

• “In the 250 years of our American Republic, no Secretary of War or Secretary of Defense has ever been impeached for carrying out lawful military operations and in our case, successful ones at that not once, War Powers resolution or not. Not under Reagan in Lebanon; not under Clinton in Kosovo; not under Obama in Iraq and Syria; not under Biden in Iraq and Syria. That’s the standard… And one disgruntled Congressman wants to shred it over policy disagreements.”

• “That’s what it is: policy disagreements not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause. The proper remedy for a policy disagreement? It’s legislation. It’s debate. It’s the next Presidential election. It’s not handing the House and Senate floor to the Democrats so that they can run a show trial against the President and the Secretary of War while Republicans still control Congress and should be delivering wins for the American people.”

• “As for the articles themselves Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen every one was a lawful operation ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress, and executed by American warriors who did their jobs.”

• “This is not about me. Politicians in Washington have accused the sailors and the pilots who struck narcoterrorist boats of war crimes for doing their job. Senators, in cute videos, have suggested the same. This resolution is the next step: put the Secretary on trial today and the men and women who carried out those orders tomorrow. If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me.”

• “We’ve seen this show before. They impeached President Trump over a perfect phone call; they impeached him again in his final week in office. Both times they failed, both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now, they’re trying a third time this time against a member of his Cabinet. They will fail again.”

• “Let’s be clear about what this resolution actually does. It tells our enemies Iran, the cartels, every adversary watching that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations… It puts a target on the backs of American warriors by signaling that Congress will undermine their missions in real time. This is not patriotism; this is sabotage.”

• “In Operation Epic Fury, by every measure, we achieved a historic military victory… We control the Strait of Hormuz. Crazy Islamists in Tehran will never, ever have a nuclear weapon. A historic effort, only made possible by a courageous Commander-in-Chief.”

• “From Day One, President Trump made homeland security national security. We sent American troops to lock down the southwest border and choked off the cartel pipeline of human smuggling, of drugs, and death. Then, we took the fight to them… Thousands of American lives saved with every drug boat sunk and every shipment prevented.”

• “President Trump gave this Department what it has not had in a generation: a Commander-in-Chief with the courage to lead and the resolve to win. I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them and I would do it again tomorrow.”

• “We will not apologize for putting American lives first. We will not apologize for stopping the flow of drugs that kill our citizens. We will not apologize for destroying the capabilities of a regime that chants ‘death to America.’”

The support for Secretary Hegseth has been swift and unambiguous:

President Donald J. Trump : “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!”

Vice President JD Vance : “Has Pete Hegseth committed impeachable crimes? The question is absurd and the answer is: obviously not. Like so much of Congress, impeachment has become a ridiculous show that stands in for actual policymaking. Congress has so many tools for registering its policy disagreements. Rather than use them, they’re going to try to impeach Pete Hegseth. They did the same to Donald Trump. Legislation is hard. Impeachments are easy (and ultimately, inconsequential). The irony is that legislators are most angry at Pete on the issues where he’s most correct: repositioning forces away from Europe/Ukraine and reorganizing the general officer corps. This isn’t about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon.”

Speaker of the House of Representatives Mike Johnson : “The impeachment effort is a political gambit for attention… The idea that you would impeach the Secretary of War at a time of international conflict sends a terrible message to our enemies and our allies, and we’re not going to play that game… It’s just purely for people to get attention, and it’s shameful.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio : “Not only did Pete execute on a direct order from the Commander-in-Chief [who], in our Constitution, is empowered and trusted with the job of keeping Americans safe, but they did it quite effectively…”

Attorney General Todd Blanche : “He is executing on President Trump’s mission… When you hear [this] rhetoric coming out of the Hill that he’s doing something illegal or wrong, that’s not true and guess what? Every single Congressman knows that… We very much support Pete and we very much support the work that he’s doing working for this Administration.”

Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins : “has defended vital U.S. interests and helped inspire record-high recruiting levels in America’s Armed Forces. He’s also been a great partner as and work together to support servicemembers as they transition to Veterans. Proud to call him a colleague and friend.”

Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum : “Together with, has overseen historically successful military operations, for which America, and the entire world, are safer. He has cut red tape to unleash innovation and modernize our military technologies. He has sent thousands of troops to secure the Southern Border. He has deployed the National Guard to make our cities, including our capital, safe again. And he has strengthened relationships with our allies to deter adversaries and protect the United States. This is America-First leadership in action.”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins : “Secretary Hegseth is doing exactly what President Trump promised for the American people: putting AMERICA FIRST and Making our Military STRONG Again. Our brave men and women in uniform deserve LEADERSHIP focused on defending our nation, not being dragged into political games. Alongside: We will stand. We will fight. We will defend this republic.”

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin : “Under the historic leadership of President Trump, has had NO stronger partner on border security than and. Together, we have locked down the border, choked off the cartels’ pipeline, and saved American lives. Pete is a patriot and a warfighter, and I am proud to call him a friend.”

Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner : “Under leadership, our military has eliminated top threats to our homeland and modernized our warfighting capabilities to protect the American people. Impeaching the Secretary of War for lawful military action sets a dangerous precedent. Congress should be focused on representing and delivering real results for the American people.”

Administrator of the Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler : “Thanks to, military recruitment has reached record highs, the U.S. has eliminated dangerous terrorists and cartel leaders around the world, our border is secure, and our warfighters are stronger than ever that’s what promised his Admin would deliver. Secretary Hegseth has also already strengthened our supply chains by recognizing that small businesses comprise over 70% of the defense industrial base and are essential to American military readiness. It is my honor to work with him on our Smaller War Plants Commission, which is making historic investments in small manufacturers to bolster our capabilities, advance innovation, and grow the Arsenal of Freedom that secures peace through strength. I’m proud to stand with and this vital mission.”

Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin : “Pete Hegseth is an American patriot and an exceptional Secretary of War! Military recruitment has been hitting record numbers and troop morale has been surging with at the tip of the spear.”

Sen. Bernie Moreno : “The idea that a failed Congressman wants to make a political point just because he’s bitter about a defeat is gross.”

Rep. Andrew Clyde : “As a 28-year Navy combat veteran, I know what it takes to protect our nation and preserve our freedoms. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has my full support.”

Rep. Randy Fine : “I trusted Pete Hegseth with my oldest son this summer when he joined the. I don’t regret that decision one bit. Thomas Massie’s almost illiterate motion is a fitting disgrace for a petulant loser. Or what I’d expect from someone with the mental capacity of a pinecone. I stand with.”

Rep. Nancy Mace : “Vote on Hegseth impeachment is at 5:30pm today I will not be voting to impeach. The Iran war is through no fault of his own and he should not be the one scapegoated for it. I fully support the changes Hegseth has made to the DoW to make our fighting force the very best it can be.”

Rep. Cory Mills : “I will be supporting our as he’s done an amazing job returning our military to its full strength and living the warrior ethos!”

Rep. Ralph Norman : “has my full support, and I remain opposed to efforts to impeach him. He has worked tirelessly to restore strength at the Department of War by putting military readiness and our warfighters FIRST. No one has done more to reestablish the strength and credibility of our military on the world stage.”

Rep. Andy Ogles : “I stand with… He’s a patriot who has delivered great results for our armed forces.”

Rep. Burgess Owens : “And for years we actually thought Massie was a ‘principled’ Republican…in the end, truth prevails. He’s always been a slick Democrat. Now an unhinged, angry one.”

Rep. William Timmons : “I stand firmly with Secretary Hegseth. Impeachment is one of the most serious powers entrusted to Congress, and Massie’s rush to bring these charges directly to the House floor treats that responsibility like a political stunt.”

Rep. Derrick Van Orden : “Massie is a shameless contrarian who is begging for attention by trying to impeach before he loses the platform he had as a member of congress. In FOURTEEN YEARS he has never got a bill signed into law. So what the hell has he been doing? Show Boating.”

Rep. Ryan Zinke : “I think it’s a classic case of showboating by a largely discredited, defeated, and disgraced lawmakerThomas Massie… I think Pete Hegseth has done a great job. This is unfortunate showboating from Thomas Massie.”

The Wall Street Journal Editorial Board : “Mr. Jeffries may think this is a free vote he can give his left-wingers before Democrats take control in January. But voters will see through this and notice that Democrats are more preoccupied with shooting at Mr. Hegseth than bringing the war in Iran to a victorious end.”

Macdonald-Laurier Institute Senior Fellow Brian L. Cox : “Hey Rep Massie. International law prof & retired military lawyer here. I read the articles of impeachment you filed against today. And it’s clear you don’t have a clue what you’re talking about… Each of the articles includes an assertion that SECWAR Hegseth ‘will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office,’ or words to that effect. In reality, the articles of impeachment are a sham from beginning to end. And it is Rep Massie, not Sec Hegseth, who IS a clear & present threat to the Constitution for abusing the impeachment powers vested in Congress by distorting international AND domestic law to create the false appearance that Hegseth’s conduct amounts to ‘high Crimes and Misdemeanors.’”

Former White House Chief of Staff Reince Priebus : “What order did Pete Hegseth order or not follow-through on that is impeachable? Massie is a grandstanding axe grinder. This is all for show… There’s nothing here.”

Former Department of Justice Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle : “The War Powers Resolution of 1973 never names the Secretary of War or imposes any duties on him. Charging Hegseth with violating it for executing the President’s orders is a farce and a waste of time. Congress could be doing real work right now instead of staging a political spectacle over a statute that does not even apply to the person they are targeting.”

Fox News Channel Legal Editor Kerri Urbahn : “These Articles of Impeachment, particularly the ones saying that Secretary Hegseth violated the federal statute that talks about notifying Congress and the like, I think they just fall so short.”

The Washington Examiner Chief Political Correspondent Byron York : “Reading through Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. There are 8 articles. Articles 1, 2, and 3 all accuse Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution by waging war in Iran. You might ask yourself: Did Pete Hegseth order US forces into action in Iran? I thought President Trump did that. That’s a good question; from the very beginning, Hegseth appears to serve as a stand-in for Massie’s real desire, which is to impeach Trump… Massie is clearly pushing these articles because he is racing the clock against his own departure from Congress on January 3, having been defeated in a Republican primary in his home state of Kentucky. There is only so much time left to do damage, and with this BS impeachment, Massie is trying to make the most of it.”

Nassau County (NY) Executive Bruce Blakeman : “On the anniversary of the Marine Corps I find it disgraceful that Thomas Massie would move to impeach Pete Hegseth a military veteran and Patriot who restored our military capabilities. Massie is a petulant and small man not worthy of serving in the House of Representatives.”

Veteran Action Founder Mark Lucas : “Side with Massie and Jeffries to impeach Pete Hegseth, and you won’t have a future in the Republican Party. is watching every vote. Vote NO.”

Veteran Action : “Thomas Massie is a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman. Veteran Action stands with. Tell Congress to vote NO on the impeachment.”

Article III Project Founder and President Mike Davis : “This Hegseth impeachment is garbage. Congress declares war. The president makes war. He can repel sudden attack. He can protect American troops, assets, and allies. He does not need a declaration of war. Where were Massie’s articles of impeachment against Lloyd Austin after Afghanistan? They won’t go after Trump. So they go after Pete. Pete Hegseth is a bold and fearless warrior for the Constitution. He is highly effective. He is doing his job. Call your House Rep. Oppose this bogus impeachment.”

Former Deputy National Security Adviser Victoria Coates : “It’s political theater at its worst because the subject is deadly serious. These are our warfighters and they’re being used as pawns. Unfortunately, I think this is a preview of what we’re going to see out of the next Democrat Congress. Congressman Massie should be ashamed of himself for trying to take advantage of these last couple of weeks for this kind of performance.”

NewsNation host Katie Pavlich : “After months of claiming they care about affordability, Democrats in Congress, along with Republican losers like Thomas Massie and Thom Tillis, have their sights focused on Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. They’re demanding impeachment, citing an array of emotional reasons and international law that doesn’t exist… Hegseth is a patriot fulfilling his oath.”

Harvard Law Professor Emeritus Alan Dershowitz : “I would be honored to help defend him because these are not impeachable offenses… None of the grounds that are in the Massie allegations come even close to meeting that standard.”

Attorney Mehek Cooke : “As an attorney my advice to: isn’t going anywhere. YOU are. SCOTUS rejected Congress bypassing the President to issue binding orders. You can’t impeach Hegseth for defying an order Congress lacked power to issue. Your articles lack legal foundation.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Will Chamberlain : “Everything about this Hegseth impeachment is like a perfect microcosm of passive-aggressiveness, cowardice, resentment, and envy.
• He’s trying to get Hegseth impeached instead of Trump, who he’s still too cowardly to go after personally.
• He’s going after Hegseth because Hegseth endorsed against him in his primary.
• He’s using legal arguments he knows are frivolous. Thomas Massie has been in the House for well over a decade, he knows concurrent resolutions are non-binding, but he’s saying that failing to defy his commander-in-chief and adhere to a non-binding Congressional resolution is an impeachable offense.
• And to top it all off, he’s saying ‘this is all for Hegseth’s own good’ with a smug insinuation that the evidence Massie does not possess will doom him.
• This, from the guy who talked about ‘how much work he and Trump still had to do together’ during his primary, and who published an out-of-date Trump endorsement when Trump had endorsed his opponent.
Thomas Massie is a weak, pathetic excuse for a man.”

Journalist Lara Logan : “The Sec of War has not committed any crime. Massie cannot possibly be so ignorant to the functioning of govt that he does not know the principal military advisors to the President on war in Iran are the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs & the Centcom Commander. So if the Iran war is his issue, he is going after the wrong man. Punishing Pete Hegseth for restoring the U.S. Military to the strength & organization needed to defend this country from all enemies both foreign & domestic is an odd choice. I relish all the attacks that will come at me for saying this bring it on. Massie is wrong.”

Samaritan’s Purse President Franklin Graham : “I believe the real reason they are coming after Secretary Hegseth is because he has taken on the anti-God, woke, and DEI initiatives that the Biden administration had pushed down the throats of our military. Since Secretary Hegseth has been at the Pentagon, he’s been cleaning houseand millions of Americans are grateful. I encourage everyone to pray for him, that God would give him strength for this difficult hour.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Josh Hammer : “Patriots stand with.”

Lieutenant Colonel Robert “Buzz” Patterson, USAF (Ret.) : “Massie is trying to impeach him and is changing our military for the better! This is huge! I support Pete. He’s a great dude and we need him.”

Center for Renewing America Executive Director Wade Miller : “The good news is that voters already impeached Massie. He was one of the biggest facilitators of big spending in DC all while he fakely postured on it to Americans. His entire sham impeachment effort is merely revenge because Trump endorsed against him. Weaponizing impeachments like this is exceedingly corrupt and Congress will now be less corrupt once Massie is out of office.”

The Dossier Publisher Jordan Schachtel : “Would be beyond absurd for any GOP rep to vote for impeachment. SecWar has done a terrific job revitalizing the military and has served his country admirably.”

Advancing American Freedom Senior Legal Fellow Hans von Spakovsky : “Massie is abusing impeachment power; it’s not intended to be used as political weapon when you disagree with policy but only for serious misconduct”

Article III Project : “Rep. Thomas Massie filed an impeachment resolution against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, and Democrats are itching to run with it. The House must kill it. Hegseth committed no treason. He took no bribe. No evidence shows corruption or any other crime.”

California Post Opinion Editor Joel Pollak : “Impeachment of a cabinet member for doing his job, even badly (not the case here), is unconstitutional. It’s why I opposed the impeachment of the (truly awful) Mayorkas under Biden. Media cheerleaders remind us they are siding with one party and with America’s enemy in wartime.”

Commentator Glenn Beck : “Pete Hegseth is everything the DC establishment hates, and that’s why they’re making him a scapegoat. He transformed the Department of War from a gay, woke, weak cesspool into a deadly fighting force once again. He has inspired our warriors to serve their country, not their ideology. He has made it clear to our enemies that the United States military will not be mocked. That is his real ‘crime’ against the establishment that was managing America’s decline. They’re trying to make this all about the Iran War. But that’s Trump’s conflict. If you think it’s an illegal war, your argument is with the man we elected as Commander-in-Chief, not the man he chose to run the department.”

Commentator Mark Levin : “Seeking the impeachment of the Secretary of War in the middle of military operations against the Iranian regime, without a single legitimate impeachable allegation, is among the evilest and most diabolical acts of any political majority/party in our history! The entire Democrat Party and a freak Republican on his way out of Congress giving aid and comfort to the enemy an enemy that has killed and maimed thousands of Americans, sought the assassination of the president and others, and will get nuclear weapons if it is not defeated. History will remember this, depending on how long this republic survives.”

America First Policy Institute : “Under leadership, the U.S. military hit a 15-YEAR recruiting high across all 5 branches. Americans are PROUD to wear the uniform and serve our great Nation.”

Tea Party Patriots Co-Founder Jenny Beth Martin : “Hegseth just laid it out. This impeachment push tells Iran and every adversary that we will punish our own warriors for winning a lawful fight. One rogue legislator with a personal grudge does not get to veto the commander in chief. This is not patriotism. This is sabotage.”

Tea Party Patriots : “The House votes at 5:30 tonight on impeaching Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary for re-election, forced the vote. ‘None of these are high crimes or misdemeanors.’ Pete Hegseth is right.”

Distributed on November 10th, 2026.

🇺🇸 Vance Frames Hegseth Impeachment Push as Symptom of Congressional Dysfunction and Resistance to Pentagon Overhaul

Vice President JD Vance dismissed the impeachment drive against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as an absurd political spectacle that masks deeper institutional anger over strategic force realignments and bureaucratic reforms rather than any high crimes tied to Iran operations.

On November 10, 2026, Vance posted that the question of whether Hegseth committed impeachable offenses is absurd and the answer is obviously not. He described impeachment as a ridiculous substitute for actual policymaking, noting that Congress possesses ample tools for registering disagreements yet opts for the easier path it previously used against President Donald Trump. Legislation requires sustained effort and compromise; impeachments generate headlines and procedural theater while remaining ultimately inconsequential. The real friction, Vance argued, centers on Hegseth's decisions to reposition forces away from Europe and Ukraine commitments while reorganizing the general officer corps. This is not primarily about Iran hostilities but about confronting entrenched Pentagon bureaucracy.

Outgoing Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed challenger and faces the end of his congressional tenure, introduced a privileged resolution containing eight articles of impeachment on November 9. The charges focus heavily on alleged violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution through continued Iran operations without specific congressional authorization or after concurrent resolutions calling for force withdrawal, alongside claims involving Yemen strikes, Venezuelan operations including the capture of Nicolás Maduro, civilian casualty minimization, and alleged retaliation against Senator Mark Kelly over speech. Massie has maintained the push is about constitutional violations rather than job performance. Hegseth, in a rare Pentagon briefing the following day, labeled the effort a farce and stunt driven by one disgruntled congressman's ego and resentment, insisting policy disagreements fall outside the founders' impeachment standards of high crimes, misdemeanors, treason, or bribery. No prior secretary of war or defense has faced impeachment for executing lawful military operations, he noted, citing precedents under multiple administrations.

Vance's framing aligns with observable patterns. Hegseth has directed roughly 20 percent reductions in generals and admirals by early 2027, framed as accountability for officers who clung to prior priorities or resisted civilian control, alongside reviews of European force posture that include canceled deployments and shifts of Ukraine support coordination toward NATO allies. These moves prioritize American resource allocation over indefinite European basing and general officer bloat. Midterm losses have fueled bipartisan unease over Iran costs, yet Vance has previously identified the war itself as a key electoral factor while defending the broader strategic pivot. Massie's timing, as a lame-duck already defeated, amplifies the perception of personal score-settling over systemic reform. Congressional majorities have historically deferred war powers enforcement to the executive across administrations; converting those recurring disputes into impeachment proceedings risks further eroding the distinction between policy debate and removal thresholds. Trump has publicly backed Hegseth, describing him as highly rated by troops and dismissing Massie as a perpetual opponent of Republican priorities. House procedural votes on the resolution were expected as early as November 10, testing whether enough Republicans join Democrats to advance the articles before the next session.

12 PM Top-of-the-Hour News

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has defiantly responded to the articles of impeachment filed by Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massie...: “It's a farce. And it's a stunt. And everybody knows it. ”
Hegseth didn't hold back on Massie...: “What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting. Is not oversight. And it's not accountability. It's a political spectacle. A personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment. Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president. ”
President Trump is backing his defense secretary...: “Massey is a loser, stone cold loser. We won two wars and we've made the world a lot safer place. ”
Trump said Hegseth should be praised, not impeached.

On Capitol Hill, House Republicans begin the process of choosing their next leaders today.
Our Stacy Lyn reports from Washington...: “House Speaker Mike Johnson is not running for minority leader. I just didn't feel after a lot of prayer and reflection, I didn't feel like that was the best thing for me to do, but says he's still committed to the House. We're focused on finishing the 119th strong. We're going to do that. I'm still in charge here until early January. He's also confident about the two Republicans competing. for the job. We have two extraordinary guys that are running to lead the conference. I'm close to both of them. The race is between current Majority Leader Steve Scalise and Congressman Jim Jordan. The results will help shape the party's leadership as Democrats prepare to take control of the House in January. Stacy Linn Worldwide News Network, Washington. ”

Inflation rose more than expected in October.
Our John Terrett reports from the business desk...: “CPI is the Consumer Price Index, a measure of inflation paid in the stores, gas stations, and for services. It rose in October 0.4%, more than the expected 0.3%. Strip out food and energy and core inflation rose at 0.3%, not the expected 0.2%. No annual comparison this time round. Because in October last year there was a government shutdown, so nothing to compare it to. The report complicates things for the Federal Reserve, which meets again in December to decide the future direction of interest rates. Wall Street has increased betting on the chance of two rate hikes now before mid-2027. John Terret, Worldwide News Network. ”

For the first time since February, the U-S, Ukraine, and Russia met in Abu Dhabi today for peace talks.  Rustern Umerov is Ukraine's lead negotiator...: “We hope that we will achieve a lasting peace for Ukraine. It is security guarantees, and we will also focus on the objectives of this meeting to come with the results with outcomes to achieve this lasting peace. ”
The three sides are scheduled to meet again tomorrow.

In Cordoba, Argentina... Pope Leo drew an estimated 650-thousand people to an outdoor mass today.  He praised Argentina's long history of Catholic devotion.
He's the first Pope to visit the country since 1987.  He will also visit Uruguay and Peru during his 12-day South American tour.

Food banks across the country are preparing to serve a growing number of Americans this Thanksgiving.
A national survey from Feeding America finds 90 percent of food banks are seeing an increased or steady demand.
This woman is at a busy food pantry in New Jersey, where an estimated 1.2 million people are facing food insecurity.: “We have here families that never went to a pantry and they are saying there is no other way that they can afford food. ”
Nationwide, it's estimated that nearly 48-million people are facing food insecurity, about one in seven households, according to USDA estimates.

The two surviving Beatles will be reuniting on stage...
Ringo Starr and Paul McCartney will join Joe Walsh's Vets Aid music festival in Las Vegas on January 29th.
McCartney and Starr last performed together in London in 2024.
